plan.rationale: Initial plan for a tall-skinny GEMM (M=32, N=4096, K=4096): no prior feedback, so use the baseline swizzle [0] to establish row-major behavior and keep full analytic weights equal. Domains include only tiles that divide M,N,K (block_M in {32,64}, since 128 does not divide 32; block_N in {64,128}; block_K in {32,64}); block_M=128 is retained in the declared domain for schema compatibility but tuples violating divisibility will be infeasible under exact tiling, so HiGHS should effectively prefer block_M=32/64. Shared-memory estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages, 4*block_M*block_N) and the hard 32768-byte portability cap should permit small-M configs while discouraging oversized footprint. Objective balances traffic, launch count, pipeline depth, and footprint; with M=32, reuse=min(swizzle or 1, ceil(M/block_M)) is at most 1 against the row-major baseline, so the analytical panel-reuse hypothesis offers no advantage initially. Hypothesis to test after feedback: enabling swizzle [4,8,16] may improve panel locality on the M=32 row dimension only if the simulator shows actual traffic/latency gains; if not, downweight traffic/reuse and favor deeper pipelining or smaller footprint. Validation scope: simulator estimates for GB10 only, not hardware measurements; Metal numerically checks the exact source/TIR/config but does not execute the CUDA binary.

Attempt-00 (block_M=32, block_N=64, block_K=32, stages=3, swizzle=0) passed all checks with simulated 147.72us, 33.82MB DRAM, 5 blocks/SM, 18KB smem. Since M=32, block_M=128 can never divide M and block_M=64 with N/K tiling would pitch tiles too large; block_M=32 is the only valid axis that divides M=32 exactly, so it is pinned. To improve utilization for this 32x4096x4096 shape we broaden swizzle to [0,4,8,16] to test the serpentine panel-reuse hypothesis against the row-major baseline, and keep block_N in {64,128} and block_K in {32,64} to explore larger tiles that should amortize A-traffic and increase AI, while num_stages is restricted to {2,3} since stages=1 under-pipelines and stages=3 already worked. shared_memory_limit stays at the 32768 hard portability cap; footprint weight kept at 1 to keep configs small enough for 5+ blocks/SM. Traffic weight raised to 1.5 because B (16M elements) dominates DRAM reads at ~33.8MB observed — reuse from swizzle would mainly affect A, so we will inspect simulated_dram_mb and simulated_us after feedback: if swizzle>0 does not reduce simulated DRAM or latency, downweight traffic to ~0.5-1.0 and steer toward block_N=128 and stages=2. Launches weight lowered to 0.5 because ceil(M/32)=1 so launch count is governed by N tiles only and is less discriminating. All choices are subject to divisibility and the estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*stages, 4*block_M*block_N) <= 32768. Scope note: simulator results are estimates, not hardware measurements; Metal numerically checks the exact source/TIR/config but does not execute the CUDA binary. This is a local hypothesis based on one observed point, not a global optimality claim.

Attempt-00 (M32/N64/K32/stages3/swz0) gave 147.72us, 33.82MB DRAM, 5 blocks/SM, 18KB smem. Attempt-01 (M32/N64/K64/stages2/swz16) gave 147.67us, identical 33.82MB DRAM, 4 blocks/SM, 24KB smem. Swizzle=16 produced no DRAM reduction and only a negligible latency change, so the serpentine panel-reuse hypothesis is not materializing on this M=32 shape; reuse is bounded by ceil(M/block_M)=1 for block_M=32. I keep swizzle [0,4,8,16] in the domain so the optimizer can still test it, but downweight traffic from 1.5 back to 1.0 since DRAM is dominated by the fixed B read and is insensitive to A locality here. block_M is pinned to 32 because M=32 must be divided and 64/128 cannot tile it. I now include block_N=128 (N=4096 divisible) to halve N-tile count and amortize A reads, keeping block_K in {32,64} and stages in {2,3}; the 32768 portability cap plus the estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*stages, 4*block_M*block_N) still bounds smem. Launches weight stays 0.5 (only ~1 launch-row since ceil(32/32)=1) and pipeline weight stays 1.5 to favor deeper overlap. Next hypothesis: block_N=128 with stages=2 or 3 may reduce simulated block count/latency versus the 64-wide points; if simulated_us stays ~flat and simulated_dram_mb is unchanged, further downweight traffic and explore block_K=64/stages=3 for pipelining rather than footprint. Scope: simulator values are GB10 estimates, not hardware measurements; Metal numerically checks exact source/TIR/config but does not execute the CUDA binary. This is a local revision from two observed points, not a global optimality claim.

Three observed points (attempt-00: 147.72us; attempt-01: 147.67us; attempt-02: 147.67us) are nearly identical in simulated latency and share exactly 33.816576 MB simulated DRAM regardless of swizzle (0/8/16) and block_K (32/64). Since reuse is capped at ceil(M/block_M)=1 for block_M=32, the serpentine panel-reuse hypothesis has no structural leverage here; swizzle cannot reduce A reloads. I therefore downweight traffic to 0.5 (it is dominated by the fixed B read and observed DRAM is invariant) and downweight footprint to 0.5 since smem has not been a binding differentiator (18KB vs 24KB both fine under the 32768 cap). block_M is pinned at 32 (M=32 must be divided exactly; 64/128 cannot tile it). block_N stays {64,128} to test whether widened N tiles reduce block count/latency; block_K {32,64} and stages {2,3} retained because stages=3 with block_K=32 already produced the best latency. Pipeline weight raised to 2 to favor deeper overlap/less K-per-stage serialization, which is the main lever observed to have any (small) effect. Launches stays 0.5 since ceil(M/32)=1 makes it nearly constant across tuples. Shared cap kept at 32768 (hard portability cap dominates the estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*stages, 4*block_M*block_N)). Next hypothesis: block_N=128 or stage-3/K-64 variants may shave the small latency gap; if DRAM and latency remain flat across new tuples, further downweight traffic/footprint and treat this shape as bandwidth-flat. Scope: simulated_us and simulated_dram_mb are GB10 simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; Metal numerically checks the exact source/TIR/config but does not execute the CUDA binary. Local revision from three observed points, not a global optimality claim.

Four observed points (attempt-00 147.72us/18KB/5 blocks-per-SM; attempts 01-03 all 147.67us/24KB/4 blocks-per-SM) are latency-flat within ~0.05us and share identical simulated DRAM 33.816576MB regardless of swizzle (0/4/8/16) or block_K (32/64). With M=32 and block_M=32, reuse=min(swizzle or 1, ceil(32/32))=1 always, so the serpentine panel-reuse hypothesis cannot reduce A reloads; DRAM is dominated by the fixed B read. I therefore keep block_M pinned to 32 (only divisor of M=32), keep swizzle [0,4,8,16] to let HiGHS still test the hypothesis, but downweight traffic to 0.5 since it is invariant across observed tuples. Pipeline weight stays 2 (deeper overlap was the only lever producing even a tiny improvement, stages=3 in attempt-00). Footprint weight raised back to 1.0 to bias toward the 18KB/stages-3/block_K-32 region (5 blocks/SM) which matched the best latency with a smaller footprint, versus the 24KB points; shared_memory_limit kept at the hard 32768-byte portability cap, and the estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages, 4*block_M*block_N) must also satisfy divisibility of N=4096, K=4096. Launches stays 0.5 because ceil(32/32)=1 makes it nearly constant. Next hypothesis: try block_N=128 and block_K=32/stages=3 combinations (not yet observed) alongside swizzle variants; if simulated_us remains ~147.7us and DRAM unchanged, treat this shape as latency/bandwidth-flat and prefer the smallest-footprint config for occupancy. Scope: simulated_us/simulated_dram_mb are GB10 simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; Metal numerically checks the exact source/TIR/config but does not execute the CUDA binary. Local revision from four observed points, not a global optimality claim.

Five observed points: attempt-00 (M32/N64/K32/stages3/swz0) = 147.72us, 18KB smem, 5 blocks/SM; attempts 01-04 (M32/N64/K64/stages2 with swz 16/8/4/0) all = 147.6675us, 24KB smem, 4 blocks/SM, identical 33.816576MB DRAM. Latency is flat within ~0.05us and DRAM is exactly invariant across swizzle 0/4/8/16 and block_K 32/64. With M=32 and block_M=32, reuse=min(swizzle or 1, ceil(32/32))=1 always, so the serpentine panel-reuse hypothesis has no structural leverage and observed DRAM confirms it does not materialize. I keep block_M pinned to 32 (only exact divisor of M=32; 64/128 cannot tile it) and retain swizzle [0,4,8,16] so the solver is not artificially narrowed. Traffic weight cut to 0.3 and launches to 0.3 because both are observed-invariant on this shape; pipeline weight kept at 1.5 to preserve favor for the stages-3/K-32 configuration that tied the best latency with the smallest footprint (18KB, 5 blocks/SM), and footprint weight kept at 1 to bias toward the high-occupancy region. shared_memory_limit stays at the hard 32768 portability cap; estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages, 4*block_M*block_N) plus exact divisibility of N=K=4096 bound feasibility. Unexplored tuples that may differentiate: block_N=128 (halves N tiles, larger B tile footprint), block_K=32 with stages=2, and block_K=64 with stages=3. Next hypothesis: block_N=128 or stages=3/K=64 combinations may shift block count/occupancy enough to break the latency plateau; if simulator remains ~147.7us with unchanged DRAM, treat the shape as latency-flat and finalize the smallest-footprint stages-3 point. Scope: simulated_us/simulated_dram_mb are GB10 simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; Metal numerically checks the exact source/TIR/config but does not execute the CUDA binary. Local revision from five observed points, not a global optimality claim.

Six observed points are latency-flat within ~0.05us (147.6675-147.7160us) and share identical 33.816576MB simulated DRAM regardless of swizzle 0/4/8/16 and block_K 32/64. With M=32 and block_M=32, reuse=min(swizzle or 1, ceil(32/32))=1 always, so the serpentine panel-reuse hypothesis has no structural leverage and observed DRAM confirms it does not materialize; traffic/launches stay downweighted (0.3 each) as they are observed-invariant. block_M pinned to 32 (only exact divisor of M=32). Retain swizzle [0,4,8,16] so the solver is not artificially narrowed. Num_stages restricted to {2,3} since both observed stage-2 (24KB, 4 blocks/SM) and stage-3 (18KB, 5 blocks/SM) points passed and stage-1 is clearly under-pipelined; pipeline weight 1.5 keeps favor for deeper overlap, footprint weight 1 biases toward the high-occupancy 18KB region. shared_memory_limit stays at the hard 32768 portability cap; estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages, 4*block_M*block_N) plus exact divisibility of N=K=4096 bound feasibility. Unexplored differentiating tuples: block_N=128 (halves N tiles, larger B tile footprint, may change block count/occupancy), block_K=64 with stages=3, and block_K=32 with stages=2. Next hypothesis: block_N=128 combinations may shift block count/occupancy enough to break the latency plateau; if simulator stays ~147.7us with unchanged DRAM, treat this shape as latency-flat and finalize the smallest-footprint stages-3 point. Scope: simulated_us/simulated_dram_mb are GB10 simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; Metal numerically checks the exact source/TIR/config but does not execute the CUDA binary. Local revision from six observed points, not a global optimality claim.

Seven observed points show a latency plateau: attempt-00 (N64/K32/stages3/swz0) 147.716us/18KB/5 blocks-per-SM, and attempts 01-06 (N64/K64/stages2 with swz 16/8/4/0, plus N64/K32/stages3 swz16/8) all 147.6675-147.7160us with identical 33.816576MB simulated DRAM. Swizzle 0/4/8/16 and block_K 32/64 do not change DRAM or latency, so the serpentine panel-reuse hypothesis is not materializing on this M=32 shape, as expected since reuse=min(swizzle or 1, ceil(M/block_M)) is bounded at 1. block_M is pinned to 32 (only exact divisor of M=32; 64/128 cannot tile M). Traffic and launches stay downweighted to 0.3 each because they are observed-invariant here. Pipeline weight 1.5 retains preference for deeper overlap (the only lever with any observed effect, stages=3 giving the tied-best and smallest-footprint 18KB/5-blocks-per-SM point). Footprint weight 1 biases toward high-occupancy small-smem configs. shared_memory_limit stays at the 32768-byte hard portability cap; estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages, 4*block_M*block_N) plus exact divisibility of N=4096 and K=4096 bound feasibility. The untested region is block_N=128 (halves N-tile count, larger B tile footprint, may change block count/occupancy) combined with block_K/stages variants; prior exclusion of earlier tuples keeps prior swizzle/stage points from being re-selected. Next hypothesis: block_N=128 configurations may break the latency plateau by reducing launch/block count; if simulator remains ~147.7us with unchanged DRAM, treat the shape as latency-flat and finalize the smallest-footprint stages-3 point. Scope: simulated_us and simulated_dram_mb are GB10 simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; Metal numerically checks the exact source/TIR/config but does not execute the CUDA binary. Local revision from seven observed points, not a global optimality claim.
